title: Backward compatibility contract for fixed model versions — prompt/output/parameter stability
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define and implement a machine-readable backward-compatibility contract for immutable/fixed model versions that we publish and enforce when customers pin to a version. The contract must cover: 1) prompt schema expectations (required fields, typing, and embedding/prefix handling), 2) deterministic output shape guarantees (message structure, function-calling outputs, and canonical error codes), 3) exposed parameter ranges and semantics (temperature, max_tokens, top_k/top_p equivalents), and 4) performance profile publishing format (latency P50/P95, token cost estimates, memory footprint). This ticket scopes the spec, test harness, gating for model replacement, and integration points for the Console and API docs.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable contract spec (JSON Schema + human-readable appendix) exists in Confluence and is linked from model onboarding flow
Unit and integration tests run in onboarding CI and exercise prompt/schema mutations, function-calling outputs, and parameter boundary values
Runtime checks validate contract compliance at model publish time; non-compliant models are blocked from 'pinned' feature until remediation
Performance profile publishing pipeline outputs P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, and token-cost estimate in the agreed telemetry format
Console shows a 'compatibility badge' and lists contract version with clear mitigations and fallback guidance
decision_notes: Use JSON Schema v2020-12 for contract encoding to leverage existing validation libraries across services
Enforce semantic versioning for contract schema (contract.v1 -> contract.v2) so pinned versions reference both model SHA and contract version

Require function-calling output to include 'rc' (result_code) and 'structured' fields for downstream parsers; free-text can still vary but must be accompanied by a machine-readable payload when function-calling is used
Do not attempt to guarantee token-level exact matches; instead guarantee stable output shape, fields, and parameter semantics to be practical across quantization/kernel changes
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize contract proto and JSON Schema; publish draft on Confluence and sync with PM and Console teams
Week 2: Implement CI validators and baseline tests in onboarding CI; add mocked model fixtures for negative tests
Week 3: Integrate runtime publish-time checks into publishing pipeline; gate 'pin to version' feature behind successful contract validation
Week 4: Enable Console display and docs; run limited internal canary with 3 enterprise customers before full rollout
QA_checks: Schema drift tests: mutate prompt/parameter shapes and assert validator rejects incompatible changes
Output shape fuzzing: run thousands of prompts against a reference pinned model and confirm structured fields are present
Performance regression: compare P50/P95 and token cost against published profile; flag >15% variance
End-to-end: pin model in staging, route requests through routing layer, confirm fallback behavior when a non-compliant variant is introduced
monitoring_alerts: ContractValidationFailure: fired when a new model publish fails contract validation
PinnedModelMismatch: when runtime responses from a pinned model omit required structured fields
PerformanceDeviation: P95 deviates >15% from published profile for more than 5m
performance_profile_publication: Fields required: model_sha, contract_version, sequence_length_distribution_sample, tokens_per_sec_estimate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, token_cost_estimate_usd_per_1k
Profiles should include measurement harness metadata: hardware type, batch sizes, concurrent clients, profiling script version
Profiles published to model catalog and attached to each pinned-version entry in the Console
